Historical findings CASEID FILE NOTE
1) Domain context:

The intake record concerns a request to facilitate marriage-based immigration status. The domain covers immigration petition processing, relationship evidence compilation, interview preparation, and disclosure obligations to immigration authorities. Records in this domain typically include petition forms, affidavits, supporting documents, and correspondence channels between applicants and officials.

2) What occurred:

The actor submitted a written request through an intake channel seeking facilitation of a paid marriage arrangement for immigration purposes. The request document specified four components: (a) identification of a willing spouse candidate, (b) creation of relationship evidence documents, (c) preparation of both parties for immigration interviews, and (d) concealment of financial compensation from immigration officers. The actor referenced specific artifacts: a named account, dated records of the relationship, and communication channels between the parties. The document included field-level specifications for evidence types (photographs, correspondence, financial records) and described the interview preparation as coaching both individuals to present a consistent narrative. The concealment instruction was documented as a discrete field within the request, specifying that payment information should not appear in any submission to immigration authorities.

3) Materials/access observed:

The intake document was submitted through a single channel (unspecified in the record). The actor referenced but did not attach: a named account identifier, a set of dated correspondence samples, a photograph index, a financial transaction record template, and an interview question outline. The actor had access to their own identity documents, the candidate spouse's anticipated documents, and a proposed payment schedule. No documents were attached to the intake; all referenced materials were described in the request fields only.

4) Indicators & artifacts:

The following artifacts and indicators are recorded: a payment schedule document with two named parties and a monetary amount field; a relationship timeline document with dated entries spanning approximately six months; a correspondence log with timestamps and channel identifiers (messaging platform, email); a photograph manifest with location metadata fields; a financial statement set showing transfers between two named accounts; an interview preparation document with Q&A pairs and scripted responses; a disclosure analysis field noting which documents would omit the payment arrangement; a candidate spouse profile with a willingness attestation field; and a coordination calendar with meeting dates and preparation session records. The concealment field explicitly designated which documents and channels would exclude reference to financial compensation. All documents were described as drafts or templates in the intake; no finalized artifacts were attached.
